title: Lecturas graduadas — Reading
intro: Textos reales graduados por nivel (A2 → C1) del mundo de la hostelería, el turismo y las ventas. Cada lectura trae una estrategia previa, un glosario desplegable, preguntas de comprensión (algunas de inferencia) y una tarea de escritura para responder al texto. Lee primero de corrido, luego responde; usa el glosario solo si te atascas.

legend.label: lectura
legend.desc: el texto graduado — léelo entero antes de responder

sections.title: Una nota de bienvenida (A2)
sections.rule: Estrategia: en textos cortos y prácticos (notas, carteles, emails), busca primero la acción que te piden y los datos clave (horas, lugares, teléfonos). No necesitas entender cada palabra.

reading.title: Welcome note in the room
reading.strategy: Vas a leer la nota que un hotel deja en la habitación. Antes de leer, pregúntate: ¿qué horarios y servicios menciona?
reading.text:
Dear Guest,

Welcome to Hotel Sol! We are delighted to have you with us.

Breakfast is served in the ground-floor restaurant from 7:00 to 10:30 every morning. If you prefer, you can order room service by dialling 9 from your phone.

The swimming pool and gym are open until 10 p.m. Please remember that check-out is at 12:00 noon. If you need a late check-out, just let reception know and we will do our best to help.

Should you need anything at all, we are here 24 hours a day. Enjoy your stay!

The Hotel Sol Team

quiz.question: 4. For a late check-out, you should…

produce.label: tu turnoEscribe una nota de bienvenida breve (3–4 frases) para la habitación de tu hotel: saluda, da el horario del desayuno y ofrece ayuda.
produce.placeholder: Ej: Dear Guest, welcome to… Breakfast is served from… If you need anything, we are here 24 hours a day. Enjoy your stay!

sections.title: Una reseña de un huésped (A2–B1)
sections.rule: Estrategia: en una reseña, distingue los puntos positivos de los negativos y fíjate en la valoración global (¿recomendaría volver?). Palabras como but, however o although marcan el cambio de tono.

reading.title: Online review — ★★★★☆
reading.strategy: Una huésped deja una reseña del hotel. Busca: ¿qué le gustó?, ¿qué no?, ¿volvería?
reading.text:
We spent three nights here and had a wonderful time overall.

The staff were the highlight of our stay — always friendly and quick to help. The receptionist even booked us a table at a lovely local restaurant. The room was spacious and spotless, and the bed was very comfortable.

However, the breakfast was a little disappointing: the coffee was cold and there wasn't much choice for vegetarians. The Wi-Fi was also quite slow in the evenings.

Despite these small issues, we would definitely come back. The location is unbeatable and the value for money is excellent. Highly recommended for a city break.

quiz.question: 1. What did the guest like most?
3. The word 'however' signals…
options: a change to a negative point

produce.label: tu turnoResponde a esta reseña como el hotel: agradece, reconoce el problema del desayuno y promete mejorar. 3–4 frases.
produce.placeholder: Ej: Thank you so much for your kind review and for highlighting our team. We're sorry the breakfast fell short — we'll address the coffee and add more vegetarian options. We'd love to welcome you back!
rubric: ¿Agradeces y mencionas algo positivo de la reseña?
¿Reconoces el punto negativo sin ponerte a la defensiva?

sections.title: Un anuncio inmobiliario (B1)
sections.rule: Estrategia: los anuncios usan lenguaje persuasivo y abreviado. Separa los hechos (tamaño, planta, precio) de los adjetivos de venta (stunning, cosy). Lee también lo que no dicen.

reading.title: Property listing — for sale
reading.strategy: Un anuncio de una vivienda en venta. Identifica: tipo, tamaño, estado y a quién va dirigido.
reading.text:
Stunning two-bedroom apartment in the heart of the old town — a rare opportunity.

This bright, south-facing flat (85 m²) has been recently refurbished to a high standard. It features an open-plan living area, a fully fitted kitchen, and a master bedroom with an en-suite bathroom. Both bedrooms have built-in wardrobes.

The property benefits from a private balcony with views over the square, as well as access to a communal garden. A parking space can be purchased separately.

Offered chain-free and move-in ready, this home would suit a professional couple or an investor seeking a strong rental return. Early viewing is strongly advised.

Asking price: €295,000.

glossary.es: sin cadena de ventas (venta directa, sin esperar)

quiz.question: 2. 'Move-in ready' means the flat…
options: needs no work before living in it

quiz.question: 4. Who is the ad aimed at?
options: a professional couple or an investor

produce.label: tu turnoEscribe un anuncio corto (4–5 frases) para una propiedad: tipo y tamaño, dos puntos fuertes, estado y una llamada a la acción.
produce.placeholder: Ej: Bright one-bedroom flat (60 m²) in a quiet, central street. Recently refurbished and move-in ready, with a fitted kitchen and a sunny balcony. Ideal for a first-time buyer. Viewing strongly advised.

¿Terminas con una llamada a la acción?

sections.title: Un email de reclamación (B1–B2)
sections.rule: Estrategia: en una queja formal, localiza (1) qué pasó, (2) cómo se siente el cliente y (3) qué pide. El tono suele ser cortés pero firme; aprende a leer la molestia 'entre líneas'.

reading.title: Email — subject: Disappointing stay (Booking #4471)
reading.strategy: Un cliente escribe tras su estancia. Pregúntate: ¿cuál es el problema principal y qué solución espera?
reading.text:
Dear Sir or Madam,

I am writing to express my dissatisfaction with a recent stay at your hotel (booking reference 4471).

Although the room itself was pleasant, we were kept awake for most of the night by building work that, we were later told, had been scheduled for weeks. At no point were we warned about this when we checked in, nor were we offered an alternative room.

When I raised the matter the following morning, the receptionist was polite but said there was 'nothing she could do'. I find this hard to accept, given that we had paid a premium rate for a quiet room.

I would appreciate a partial refund as a gesture of goodwill. I look forward to your prompt reply.

Yours faithfully,
A. Morgan

quiz.question: 1. What was the main problem?
options: Noise from building work at night

quiz.question: 2. Were the guests warned at check-in?
3. Why is the guest especially annoyed?
options: They paid a premium for a quiet room

quiz.question: 4. What does the guest want?
options: A free upgrade for next time

quiz.question: 5. The tone of the email is best described as…

produce.label: tu turnoResponde al email como el hotel: discúlpate, explica brevemente y ofrece una solución concreta (p. ej. el reembolso parcial). Tono formal.
produce.placeholder: Ej: Dear Mr/Ms Morgan, thank you for taking the time to write, and please accept our sincere apologies… We should have warned you and offered an alternative room. As a gesture of goodwill, we would be happy to refund…
rubric: ¿Te disculpas con sinceridad y reconoces el fallo?

notes.text: Fíjate en el cierre: Yours faithfully se usa cuando empiezas con 'Dear Sir or Madam' (sin nombre); Yours sincerely cuando conoces el nombre (Dear Mr Morgan). Es un detalle que marca nivel en cartas formales.

sections.title: Tendencias en el turismo (B2)
sections.rule: Estrategia: en un texto informativo, identifica la idea principal de cada párrafo y cómo se conectan. No te pierdas en los datos: busca la tesis y los ejemplos que la apoyan.

reading.title: Article — The rise of 'slow travel'
reading.strategy: Un breve artículo sobre una tendencia turística. Busca: ¿qué es 'slow travel', por qué crece y qué implica para los hoteles?
reading.text:
For decades, tourism was sold on quantity: as many cities, sights and photos as a week would allow. Increasingly, however, travellers are embracing the opposite — a movement known as 'slow travel'.

Rather than rushing between landmarks, slow travellers stay longer in one place, favour local businesses and seek authentic experiences over tick-box sightseeing. A growing awareness of the environmental footprint of frequent flights has only accelerated the trend.

For the hospitality industry, this shift brings both challenges and opportunities. Hotels that once competed on price now find that guests will pay a premium for a sense of place: locally sourced food, partnerships with nearby artisans, and staff who can share genuine recommendations.

In short, the destination is no longer just a backdrop. For a new generation of guests, how they travel matters as much as where.

quiz.question: 1. 'Slow travel' means…
options: staying longer and going deeper in fewer places
visiting as many places as possible

quiz.question: 3. According to the text, guests now…
options: will pay more for a 'sense of place'
only care about the lowest price

quiz.question: 4. 'The destination is no longer just a backdrop' means…
options: the experience matters, not only the place

quiz.question: 5. The writer's overall attitude to slow travel is…

produce.label: tu turnoResume el artículo en 2–3 frases con tus palabras y añade tu opinión: ¿cómo podría tu hotel atraer a un 'slow traveller'?
produce.placeholder: Ej: The article argues that travellers increasingly value depth over quantity… To attract slow travellers, we could partner with local producers and train staff to give authentic recommendations.
rubric: ¿Captas la idea principal con tus propias palabras (sin copiar)?

sections.title: El arte de la hospitalidad (B2–C1)
sections.rule: Estrategia: en un texto de opinión, separa el hecho de la valoración del autor, y detecta el tono (irónico, admirativo, crítico). Las ideas clave suelen ir al principio y al final de cada párrafo.

reading.title: Opinion — What hospitality really means
reading.strategy: Un columnista reflexiona sobre la hospitalidad. Pregúntate: ¿cuál es su tesis y con qué contrasta la 'buena' de la 'gran' hospitalidad?
reading.text:
Anyone can follow a script. The difference between good service and genuine hospitality lies precisely in what the script cannot anticipate.

Good service is transactional: the guest asks, the staff deliver, the box is ticked. It is necessary, but it is also forgettable. Great hospitality, by contrast, is anticipatory. It notices the guest shivering in the lobby and brings a blanket before being asked; it remembers that a returning couple celebrated their anniversary last year.

This cannot be mandated from above. No policy manual, however thick, can legislate warmth. What it requires is a culture in which staff feel trusted to use their judgement — and, crucially, are not punished for the occasional misstep that such initiative inevitably brings.

The paradox, then, is this: the most memorable moments of a stay are often the ones no manager could ever have planned. The best hotels do not script hospitality; they hire for it and then get out of the way.

quiz.question: 1. The writer's main thesis is that genuine hospitality…
3. What does great hospitality require, according to the author?
options: a culture that trusts staff to use their judgement

quiz.question: 4. 'No policy manual can legislate warmth' means…
options: warmth can't be imposed by rules

quiz.question: 5. 'Hire for it and then get out of the way' implies managers should…
options: choose the right people and let them act
